## Tracker output grammar

Must match `formatStatus` in the phase-tracker and plan-tracker extensions.

```
Phases:
  ✓ brainstorm
  → implement(W2)
  ○ verify (reason)
```

Glyphs `✓` complete, `→` in_progress, `⊘` skipped, `○` pending; `(reason)` suffix when
set; `name(substep)` only on the in-progress phase.

```
Plan: 2/5 done (1 in progress, 2 pending)

  ✓ [0] <name>
  → [1] <name>
```

or `No plan active.`. Task glyphs `✓` complete, `→` in_progress, `✗` failed, `⊘` skipped,
`○` pending, mapping 1:1 onto `plan_tracker init` `{name, status}` statuses.

For ledger task rows, match the suffix pattern `^(row \d+(?: \(\S+\))?) \| .+$` against the text after `[i] ` and restore only capture 1. Treat everything after the first canonical name's ` | ` as display text, including pipes and row-like text; never derive identity from the description. For example, `row 3 | 2/5: Verify loop behavior and recovery` restores `row 3`. Retain legacy plain names and the numeric prefix form: remove the prefix pattern `^\d+/\d+: ` only when the remainder matches the canonical pattern `^row \d+(?: \(\S+\))?$`. Strip recognized labels before verify/ship `plan_tracker init` and snapshot name comparisons. Keep Gn and every other task name byte-identical, including numeric prefixes on non-ledger names. Never restore labels from a brief: the post-restore refresh recomputes descriptions and allowance from the current spec and ledger, so a changed description or denominator is not drift or a second task.

Parse stops (print the offending line, make no tracker call):

- a task line not matching `^\s*[✓→✗⊘○] \[\d+\] .+$` - the "unparsable process-state
  task line" stop;
- a process-state section whose phase block shows all `○` - contradictory (the producer
  emits the section only with an in-progress phase);
- a phase block with more than one `→` line - contradictory (the tracker holds one active
  phase; print both lines).

## Process-state restore

Before any tracker write, read the optional ordered PR pairs. Fetch branch identity
from the first pair only (home) with
`gh pr view <N> --repo <owner/repo> --json headRefName`. Compare `headRefName` with
`git -C <worktree> branch --show-current`. A mismatch stops with
`brief names PR #N on <headRefName>, worktree is on <branch>`, substituting the observed PR number and both actual branch names, never literal placeholders; a failed fetch stops
with its error. Do not fetch later pairs' branches for this identity check.
Read the worktree spec's `## Rework record` and compare its top-level `PR:` identities
(without titles) with the brief identities in order. A mismatch stops with
`brief lists <brief order>, record lists <record order>`, substituting both observed
ordered lists, before any tracker call. Resolve the spec through reconstruction's
candidate rules below before this comparison; artifact presence supplies no approval.
Carry all paired full pre-rework heads downstream in their original order.
Carry the optional full rework base downstream; reconstruction prefers it over the first pair's head as its scan base. Without optional pairs,
retain ordinary restoration.
Preserve the entry checks, standing-grant validation, plan repair, and task snapshot;
PR identity implies no approval or gate evidence.

Facts that fix the order (from the extensions):

- Arming happens only on `start brainstorm`; `reset` disarms; `skip` and `complete`
  preserve it.
- `plan_check` stamps only inside an armed flow; unarmed it returns
  `PASS (no flow to stamp)`.
- `start implement` is rejected without a current `plan_check` stamp.
- `skip` has no state precondition and takes a `reason`; one phase is active at a time.
- `complete verify` is blocked without a fresh `conformance-reviewer` dispatch when
  closure review is enforced.
- `plan_tracker init` on an in-progress implement with every task `complete`/`skipped`
  auto-completes implement.

| Global or contamination rows (`Baseline: worktree dirty`, `Baseline: in-flight source edits`, `dirtied tracked source`, `moved HEAD`) | Take writing-plans step 6's restore-and-rerun path, not the menu. Name paths and causes; the parent's own in-flight work uses its own commit step (doc-only paths can be listed under `In-flight:`); ask the human to commit, discard, or move other paths and test-produced dirt. Never clean automatically. After restoration re-dispatch with `Findings: rerun baseline`, then parent check. |
| Other substantive `open-questions` rows (contract questions) | Present the rows, wait for answers, re-dispatch per step 3 with answers in `Findings:`, then parent check and this same return route. |
| Other checks | Use the citation table and its three-round rollback below. |

End a turn awaiting selection, restoration, or answers with phase `plan` retained in_progress and no tracker initialization of any kind. Keep the snapshot for the eventual return. Resolved failure rows disappear only through the writer's Baseline rerun; resume writes no Open Questions rows. Plans without `baseline:` bullets intentionally enter this continuation on their `baseline-line` finding.

### Citation repair

Record the plan's state before any write: tracked and clean when `git -C <worktree> ls-files --error-unmatch -- <plan path>` exits 0 and `git -C <worktree> status --porcelain -- <plan path>` prints nothing (index and working copy both match HEAD; a staged edit alone makes it dirty); otherwise copy the file to a temp path outside the repository before citation repair writes anything. Any non-empty porcelain output, including staged-only `M  <plan path>`, takes this copy path even when tracked and the working copy equals HEAD. Never substitute `git checkout` for the dirty or untracked plan's snapshot or saved-copy restore.

Classify every finding against the table by its `check` and `reason`, gathering the row's evidence first. One finding with no row -> stop (below) before any write.

| Finding (`check`, `reason`) | Evidence | Edit |
|---|---|---|
| `anchor-resolution`, range outside section or line shift | the anchor's heading string matches exactly one current spec heading | set the `**Spec:**` `L<n>-L<m>` range to the current span of that section that holds the task body's existing literals |
| `quote-integrity`, task-owned row | the row's anchor already resolves (repair anchors first) | add the missing backtick literal to the owning task's body; never replace or remove task text |
| `quote-integrity`, `Verification`-owned row | as above | add the missing literal to the header `**Verification:**` line |
| `table-closure`, row anchor not in the owner's `**Spec:**` set | the owner cell names an existing task whose body does the row's requirement | move the row's anchor together with that same owner's `**Spec:**` anchor; the owner cell never changes |
| `paths-exist`, `Modify: path "<p>" does not exist` | the owning task is `complete` or `skipped` in the task list, and `git -C <worktree> log --diff-filter=D --format=%h -1 -- <p>` is non-empty | drop that `Modify:` row |
| `paths-exist` or `tests-block`, a `Test:` path that does not exist or a `Tests:` segment not anchored | `git -C <worktree> log --diff-filter=R --format= --name-status -M -1 -- <old> <new>` shows the rename `<old>` -> `<new>` | substitute `<new>` for `<old>` in the `Test:` line and in the `Tests:` command; nothing else in the command changes |

Every other `check` (`input`, `placeholder-scan`, `header-entrypoint`, `header-happy-path`, `waiver-literal`, `wave-file-disjointness`, `internal`) and every reason not listed (a missing `Files:` block, an invalid or empty glob, a missing or ambiguous heading, a `pending`/`in_progress` owner of a dead `Modify:` row, a command broadening) has no row. Task names, count, order, wave membership, `Solo:` lines, the owner column, and task text beyond an added literal or a substituted path never change.

Loop: write every classified edit, re-run `plan_check({ planPath })`, classify any new finding the same way; at most 3 rounds.

PASS with the plan tracked and clean before the loop -> read [commit-message.md](../../finishing-a-development-branch/reference/commit-message.md), take the entire subject verbatim from its Plan citation repair row, and commit the plan alone with that message on stdin:

```bash
git -C <worktree> add -- <plan path> && git -C <worktree> commit -q -F - -- <plan path>
```

A failed commit stops with git's output. PASS with the plan untracked or dirty before the loop -> leave the repair in the working copy; it lands with the next task commit. Then continue the originating route: the call table from `skip plan R`, or reconstruction step 3.

Stop (a finding with no row, or a finding surviving the third round): when a round wrote the plan, restore its pre-loop bytes (`git -C <worktree> checkout -- <plan path>` when tracked and clean, else the saved copy) - a stop before the first write runs no git command; print the findings (a dead `Modify:` row prefixed with its owning task, e.g. `Task 5:`), leave `plan` in_progress with no `init`, and print one line:

- no row: `Repair stopped: <check> - <reason> is outside citation repair; the plan file is unchanged. Edit the plan (task changes allowed), then re-run /skill:gauntlet-resume.`
- third round: `Repair stopped: <check> - <reason> survived 3 rounds. Edit the plan, then re-run /skill:gauntlet-resume.`

Resume never edits the spec or writes an Open Question itself; the dispatched plan-writer owns generated baseline rows.

"Exact" restoration binds: the active phase identity and substep, and the plan task list
(names, order, statuses) verbatim. Prior phases show `⊘ (resume: ...)` regardless of the
brief's glyph - skip-arming is the mechanism and completing priors would fabricate gated
history. For a ledger, restore the saved mixed list only on verify/ship, then refresh its ledger entries from disk; on implement, refresh without `init`. `No plan active.` -> no `init` call; a ledger still refreshes.

Before `init`, validate feasibility against the tracker's own rules:

- pending-suffix order - every `○` task must trail every non-pending task;
- the implement auto-complete edge - an implement brief whose tasks are all
  complete/skipped is infeasible as stated; propose verify as the target and ask.

Every restore ends with:

```
Gate history not restored; re-validating `<task>` before any stage advance
```

For a ledger, use `ledger rows` as `<task>` and render the current rows and last decision from disk.

For a task plan, `<task>` is the brief's `Active task`, else the first in-progress task, else `none`
(whole-deliverable re-validation). Gate history, closure-review evidence, and fix rounds
are never inferred or restored; a ship-stage brief resumes at verify.

A restore that ran `## Plan repair` prints `Repaired plan: <n> findings (<comma-separated check names, deduplicated>)` on its own line directly before the closing line; the `Standing grant` line (SKILL.md "Post-restore continuation") keeps its place after the closing line. A first-check PASS prints no receipt and makes no commit.

# Handoff brief contract (gauntlet-resume + gauntlet-handoff supplementary)

Consumed by `gauntlet-resume/SKILL.md` (consumer) and `gauntlet-handoff/SKILL.md`
(producer). Grammar lives only here; both skills cite this file and inline none of it
(`scripts/ci.mjs` drift lint). Coupled to pi-cohort's `handoff` skill (pi-cohort >= 7.1.0, #18)
for exactly six headings - `# Handoff:`, `## Intent`, `## Repo state`, `## Decisions`,
`## Open questions`, `## Skills loaded` - and the `## Repo state` fields. `## Process
state` grammar and its consumer rules are owned here. Cohort drift is reconciled here
and nowhere else.

## Brief grammar

Headings, fixed order. A consumer keys on headings, never prose.

```markdown
# Handoff: <one line>
## Intent
## Repo state
## Decisions
## Open questions
## Skills loaded
## Process state
```

| Section | Content | Presence |
|---|---|---|
| `## Repo state` | one field per line: `toplevel`, `worktree: yes <path>` or `worktree: no`, `branch` (`detached` when none), `HEAD`, `base` (`unknown` when no remote resolves), `dirty: <porcelain>` or `dirty: clean`, `diff-stat` (`unavailable` when base unknown), `test cmd`; any field `unavailable` when its command failed; heading `## Repo state: not a git repo` outside git | always |
| `## Decisions` | bullets; rejected alternatives marked `rejected:` | always |
| `## Skills loaded` | frontmatter `name`s; `## Skills loaded: none` when none | always |
| `## Process state` | `phase_tracker status` then `plan_tracker status` verbatim; `Active task: <name|none>`; optional one or more consecutive `PR: <owner/repo#N>` / `Pre-rework head: <40-char sha>` pairs, one per record group, home first, in record order, only for a PR subject; optional single `Rework base: <40-char sha>` after all PR pairs; optional coordinated block defined below after that line; the line `Gate history not restored - re-validate before advancing.` | only when a phase is `in_progress` and no hotfix flow is in context |

For a loop ledger (line 1 exactly `# Ledger - loop engine`), replace `Active task` with these two fields, retaining both tracker status outputs and the gate-history line:

```text
Ledger: <path>
Last decision: <line>
```

Use the ledger path relative to the worktree and the last physical decision line, or `none` for an empty Decisions section. Read the ledger on disk; the brief is a pointer, not a second ledger state carrier. Permit task rows beside a ledger: copy `plan_tracker status` verbatim, including the dispatched row's `in_progress` status and any conformance tasks with their observed statuses. Never infer task state from the brief's prose. Reject a block mixing these fields with `Active task` or missing either loop field.

Consumer rules: process state absent -> plain handoff (the consumer starts its
own process from `## Intent`). Give valid ledger fields precedence over `No plan active.` and run ledger admission. Restore phase-only state for `No plan active.` only with no `Ledger` field. Load named skills as the consumer.

A brief is any text whose first line starts `# Handoff:` - a file on disk or pasted
inline. `## Repo state` is matched by prefix: `## Repo state` or
`## Repo state: not a git repo`.

## Producers

`gauntlet-handoff` is the only writer of `## Process state`; it appends to the file
cohort's `handoff` skill wrote, which ends at `## Skills loaded`. Drop exactly the last
line of the `phase_tracker status` output when it starts with `Context: `; copy the
rest verbatim. Layout, byte-exact: one blank line, the heading on its own line, a
blank line, that phase status, a blank line, the `plan_tracker status` output
verbatim, a blank line,
`Active task: <name|none>`, then, only for a PR subject, one or more consecutive
`PR: <owner/repo#N>` / `Pre-rework head: <40-char sha>` pairs, one per record group,
home first, in record order, then optional single `Rework base: <40-char sha>` after all PR pairs, then the optional coordinated block below, then the gate-history line after the last pair, rework-base line, or block -
unfenced, nothing after.
For a task plan, set `Active task` to the first `→` task name, else `none` (also for `No plan active.`). For a line-1 ledger, read its path and last decision and use the loop alternative above, retaining the optional PR pairs and rework base before the gate-history line. Copy the full rework base only from the top-level record when present; never invent a boundary for incomplete sync. Copy only top-level record pairs, without titles; `Threads:` and record `### PR #<N>` subsections are not brief fields. For N=1 emit one pair; without a Rework record use the ordinary layout.

## Tracker output grammar

Must match `formatStatus` in the phase-tracker and plan-tracker extensions.

```
Phases:
  ✓ brainstorm
  → implement(W2)
  ○ verify (reason)
```

Glyphs `✓` complete, `→` in_progress, `⊘` skipped, `○` pending; `(reason)` suffix when
set; `name(substep)` only on the in-progress phase.

```
Plan: 2/5 done (1 in progress, 2 pending)

  ✓ [0] <name>
  → [1] <name>
```

or `No plan active.`. Task glyphs `✓` complete, `→` in_progress, `✗` failed, `⊘` skipped,
`○` pending, mapping 1:1 onto `plan_tracker init` `{name, status}` statuses.

For ledger task rows, match the suffix pattern `^(row \d+(?: \(\S+\))?) \| .+$` against the text after `[i] ` and restore only capture 1. Treat everything after the first canonical name's ` | ` as display text, including pipes and row-like text; never derive identity from the description. For example, `row 3 | 2/5: Verify loop behavior and recovery` restores `row 3`. Retain legacy plain names and the numeric prefix form: remove the prefix pattern `^\d+/\d+: ` only when the remainder matches the canonical pattern `^row \d+(?: \(\S+\))?$`. Strip recognized labels before verify/ship `plan_tracker init` and snapshot name comparisons. Keep Gn and every other task name byte-identical, including numeric prefixes on non-ledger names. Never restore labels from a brief: the post-restore refresh recomputes descriptions and allowance from the current spec and ledger, so a changed description or denominator is not drift or a second task.

Parse stops (print the offending line, make no tracker call):

- a task line not matching `^\s*[✓→✗⊘○] \[\d+\] .+$` - the "unparsable process-state
  task line" stop;
- a process-state section whose phase block shows all `○` - contradictory (the producer
  emits the section only with an in-progress phase);
- a phase block with more than one `→` line - contradictory (the tracker holds one active
  phase; print both lines).

## Process-state restore

Before any tracker write, read the optional ordered PR pairs. Fetch branch identity
from the first pair only (home) with
`gh pr view <N> --repo <owner/repo> --json headRefName`. Compare `headRefName` with
`git -C <worktree> branch --show-current`. A mismatch stops with
`brief names PR #N on <headRefName>, worktree is on <branch>`, substituting the observed PR number and both actual branch names, never literal placeholders; a failed fetch stops
with its error. Do not fetch later pairs' branches for this identity check.
Read the worktree spec's `## Rework record` and compare its top-level `PR:` identities
(without titles) with the brief identities in order. A mismatch stops with
`brief lists <brief order>, record lists <record order>`, substituting both observed
ordered lists, before any tracker call. Resolve the spec through reconstruction's
candidate rules below before this comparison; artifact presence supplies no approval.
Carry all paired full pre-rework heads downstream in their original order.
Carry the optional full rework base downstream; reconstruction prefers it over the first pair's head as its scan base. Without optional pairs,
retain ordinary restoration.
Preserve the entry checks, standing-grant validation, plan repair, and task snapshot;
PR identity implies no approval or gate evidence.

Facts that fix the order (from the extensions):

- Arming happens only on `start brainstorm`; `reset` disarms; `skip` and `complete`
  preserve it.
- `plan_check` stamps only inside an armed flow; unarmed it returns
  `PASS (no flow to stamp)`.
- `start implement` is rejected without a current `plan_check` stamp.
- `skip` has no state precondition and takes a `reason`; one phase is active at a time.
- `complete verify` is blocked without a fresh `conformance-reviewer` dispatch when
  closure review is enforced.
- `plan_tracker init` on an in-progress implement with every task `complete`/`skipped`
  auto-completes implement.

Record the plan's state before any write: tracked and clean when `git -C <worktree> ls-files --error-unmatch -- <plan path>` exits 0 and `git -C <worktree> status --porcelain -- <plan path>` prints nothing (index and working copy both match HEAD; a staged edit alone makes it dirty); otherwise copy the file to a temp path outside the repository before citation repair writes anything. Any non-empty porcelain output, including staged-only `M  <plan path>`, takes this copy path even when tracked and the working copy equals HEAD. Never substitute `git checkout` for the dirty or untracked plan's snapshot or saved-copy restore.

Classify every finding against the table by its `check` and `reason`, gathering the row's evidence first. One finding with no row -> stop (below) before any write.

| Finding (`check`, `reason`) | Evidence | Edit |
|---|---|---|
| `anchor-resolution`, range outside section or line shift | the anchor's heading string matches exactly one current spec heading | set the `**Spec:**` `L<n>-L<m>` range to the current span of that section that holds the task body's existing literals |
| `quote-integrity`, task-owned row | the row's anchor already resolves (repair anchors first) | add the missing backtick literal to the owning task's body; never replace or remove task text |
| `quote-integrity`, `Verification`-owned row | as above | add the missing literal to the header `**Verification:**` line |
| `table-closure`, row anchor not in the owner's `**Spec:**` set | the owner cell names an existing task whose body does the row's requirement | move the row's anchor together with that same owner's `**Spec:**` anchor; the owner cell never changes |
| `paths-exist`, `Modify: path "<p>" does not exist` | the owning task is `complete` or `skipped` in the task list, and `git -C <worktree> log --diff-filter=D --format=%h -1 -- <p>` is non-empty | drop that `Modify:` row |
| `paths-exist` or `tests-block`, a `Test:` path that does not exist or a `Tests:` segment not anchored | `git -C <worktree> log --diff-filter=R --format= --name-status -M -1 -- <old> <new>` shows the rename `<old>` -> `<new>` | substitute `<new>` for `<old>` in the `Test:` line and in the `Tests:` command; nothing else in the command changes |

Every other `check` (`input`, `placeholder-scan`, `header-entrypoint`, `header-happy-path`, `waiver-literal`, `wave-file-disjointness`, `internal`) and every reason not listed (a missing `Files:` block, an invalid or empty glob, a missing or ambiguous heading, a `pending`/`in_progress` owner of a dead `Modify:` row, a command broadening) has no row. Task names, count, order, wave membership, `Solo:` lines, the owner column, and task text beyond an added literal or a substituted path never change.

PASS with the plan tracked and clean before the loop -> read [commit-message.md](../../finishing-a-development-branch/reference/commit-message.md), take the entire subject verbatim from its Plan citation repair row, and commit the plan alone with that message on stdin:

```bash
git -C <worktree> add -- <plan path> && git -C <worktree> commit -q -F - -- <plan path>
```

A failed commit stops with git's output. PASS with the plan untracked or dirty before the loop -> leave the repair in the working copy; it lands with the next task commit. Then continue the originating route: the call table from `skip plan R`, or reconstruction step 3.

#### Conversion recipe

Run from the supplied home worktree after step 4.2 reaches a clean, tuple-free allowance ledger. Set `ledger_path` to its repo-relative path and `conversion_subject` to the shared Returns conversion on resume sentence. Require Python 3; on an unavailable interpreter stop before writing. Use this recipe for the conversion commit, not a second hand-written edit or commit. Stop on a failed command and retain its error and working state.

Set `CHECKOUT` to the resolved home worktree's absolute path and `ledger_path` to its repo-relative ledger path.

<!-- ledger-conversion-shell -->
```bash
python3 - "$CHECKOUT" "$ledger_path" "$conversion_subject" <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import sys

checkout, path, subject = sys.argv[1:]
ledger = Path(checkout) / path

def git(*args, **kwargs):
    return subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", checkout, *args], text=True, **kwargs)

text = ledger.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
header_text = text.split("\n|", 1)[0]
if re.search(r"^returned:", header_text, re.M):
    sys.exit(0)
if git("status", "--porcelain"):
    sys.exit("returns conversion requires a clean tree")
if re.search(r"^pending:", header_text, re.M):
    sys.exit("finish pending recovery before returns conversion")

def field(snapshot, name, pattern):
    values = re.findall(r"^" + name + r": (.*)$", snapshot.split("\n|", 1)[0], re.M)
    if len(values) != 1 or not re.fullmatch(pattern, values[0]):
        sys.exit("cannot convert ledger: malformed " + name)
    return values[0]

base = field(text, "base", r"[0-9a-f]{40}")
allowance = field(text, "allowance", r"[1-9][0-9]*")
markers = {"loop: repair seed": "repair seed", "loop: repair verification": "repair verification"}
decisions = []
for line in git("log", "--reverse", "--format=%H %s", base + "..HEAD").splitlines():
    sha, old_subject = line.split(" ", 1)
    if old_subject not in markers:
        continue
    snapshot = git("show", sha + ":" + path)
    count = field(snapshot, "iterations", r"0|[1-9][0-9]*")
    if int(count) > 9007199254740991:
        sys.exit("cannot convert ledger: unsafe iterations at " + sha)
    body = git("show", "-s", "--format=%b", sha).splitlines()
    reason = (body[0] if body and body[0] else "converted").replace("|", r"\|")
    decisions.append(markers[old_subject] + " | " + reason + " | converted " + sha[:7])
if text.count("\n## Decisions\n") != 1:
    sys.exit("cannot convert ledger: missing or duplicate Decisions section")
converted = re.sub(r"^allowance: " + allowance + r"$", r"\g<0>\nreturned: none", text, count=1, flags=re.M)
if decisions:
    converted += ("" if converted.endswith("\n") else "\n") + "\n".join(decisions) + "\n"
ledger.write_bytes(converted.encode("utf-8"))
git("add", "--", path)
git("commit", "-q", "-F", "-", "--", path, input=subject + "\n")
PY
```

def field(snapshot, name, pattern):
    values = re.findall(r"^" + name + r": (.*)$", snapshot.split("\n|", 1)[0], re.M)
    if len(values) != 1 or not re.fullmatch(pattern, values[0]):

    sha, old_subject = line.split(" ", 1)

        continue
    snapshot = git("show", sha + ":" + path)
    count = field(snapshot, "iterations", r"0|[1-9][0-9]*")
    if int(count) > 9007199254740991:
        sys.exit("cannot convert ledger: unsafe iterations at " + sha)
    body = git("show", "-s", "--format=%b", sha).splitlines()
    reason = (body[0] if body and body[0] else "converted").replace("|", r"\|")
    decisions.append(markers[old_subject] + " | " + reason + " | converted " + sha[:7])
if text.count("\n## Decisions\n") != 1:
    sys.exit("cannot convert ledger: missing or duplicate Decisions section")
converted = re.sub(r"^allowance: " + allowance + r"$", r"\g<0>\nreturned: none", text, count=1, flags=re.M)
if decisions:
    converted += ("" if converted.endswith("\n") else "\n") + "\n".join(decisions) + "\n"
ledger.write_bytes(converted.encode("utf-8"))
git("add", "--", path)
git("commit", "-q", "-F", "-", "--", path, input=subject + "\n")

#### Conversion recipe

Run from the supplied home worktree after step 4.2 reaches a clean, tuple-free allowance ledger. Set `ledger_path` to its repo-relative path and `conversion_subject` to the shared Returns conversion on resume sentence. Require Python 3; on an unavailable interpreter stop before writing. Use this recipe for the conversion commit, not a second hand-written edit or commit. Stop on a failed command and retain its error and working state.

Set `CHECKOUT` to the resolved home worktree's absolute path and `ledger_path` to its repo-relative ledger path.

<!-- ledger-conversion-shell -->
```bash
python3 - "$CHECKOUT" "$ledger_path" "$conversion_subject" <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import sys

checkout, path, subject = sys.argv[1:]
ledger = Path(checkout) / path

def git(*args, **kwargs):
    return subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", checkout, *args], text=True, **kwargs)

text = ledger.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
header_text = text.split("\n|", 1)[0]
if re.search(r"^returned:", header_text, re.M):
    sys.exit(0)
if git("status", "--porcelain"):
    sys.exit("returns conversion requires a clean tree")
if re.search(r"^pending:", header_text, re.M):
    sys.exit("finish pending recovery before returns conversion")

def field(snapshot, name, pattern):
    values = re.findall(r"^" + name + r": (.*)$", snapshot.split("\n|", 1)[0], re.M)
    if len(values) != 1 or not re.fullmatch(pattern, values[0]):
        sys.exit("cannot convert ledger: malformed " + name)
    return values[0]

base = field(text, "base", r"[0-9a-f]{40}")
allowance = field(text, "allowance", r"[1-9][0-9]*")
markers = {"loop: repair seed": "repair seed", "loop: repair verification": "repair verification"}
decisions = []
for line in git("log", "--reverse", "--format=%H %s", base + "..HEAD").splitlines():
    sha, old_subject = line.split(" ", 1)
    if old_subject not in markers:
        continue
    snapshot = git("show", sha + ":" + path)
    count = field(snapshot, "iterations", r"0|[1-9][0-9]*")
    if int(count) > 9007199254740991:
        sys.exit("cannot convert ledger: unsafe iterations at " + sha)
    body = git("show", "-s", "--format=%b", sha).splitlines()
    reason = (body[0] if body and body[0] else "converted").replace("|", r"\|")
    decisions.append(markers[old_subject] + " | " + reason + " | converted " + sha[:7])
if text.count("\n## Decisions\n") != 1:
    sys.exit("cannot convert ledger: missing or duplicate Decisions section")
converted = re.sub(r"^allowance: " + allowance + r"$", r"\g<0>\nreturned: none", text, count=1, flags=re.M)
if decisions:
    converted += ("" if converted.endswith("\n") else "\n") + "\n".join(decisions) + "\n"
ledger.write_bytes(converted.encode("utf-8"))
git("add", "--", path)
git("commit", "-q", "-F", "-", "--", path, input=subject + "\n")
PY
```

from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
import sys

checkout, path, subject = sys.argv[1:]
ledger = Path(checkout) / path

def git(*args, **kwargs):
    return subprocess.check_output(["git", "-C", checkout, *args], text=True, **kwargs)

text = ledger.read_bytes().decode("utf-8")
header_text = text.split("\n|", 1)[0]
if re.search(r"^returned:", header_text, re.M):
    sys.exit(0)
if git("status", "--porcelain"):
    sys.exit("returns conversion requires a clean tree")
if re.search(r"^pending:", header_text, re.M):
    sys.exit("finish pending recovery before returns conversion")

def field(snapshot, name, pattern):
    values = re.findall(r"^" + name + r": (.*)$", snapshot.split("\n|", 1)[0], re.M)
    if len(values) != 1 or not re.fullmatch(pattern, values[0]):
        sys.exit("cannot convert ledger: malformed " + name)
    return values[0]

base = field(text, "base", r"[0-9a-f]{40}")
allowance = field(text, "allowance", r"[1-9][0-9]*")
markers = {"loop: repair seed": "repair seed", "loop: repair verification": "repair verification"}
decisions = []
for line in git("log", "--reverse", "--format=%H %s", base + "..HEAD").splitlines():
    sha, old_subject = line.split(" ", 1)
    if old_subject not in markers:
        continue
    snapshot = git("show", sha + ":" + path)
    count = field(snapshot, "iterations", r"0|[1-9][0-9]*")
    if int(count) > 9007199254740991:
        sys.exit("cannot convert ledger: unsafe iterations at " + sha)
    body = git("show", "-s", "--format=%b", sha).splitlines()
    reason = (body[0] if body and body[0] else "converted").replace("|", r"\|")
    decisions.append(markers[old_subject] + " | " + reason + " | converted " + sha[:7])
if text.count("\n## Decisions\n") != 1:
    sys.exit("cannot convert ledger: missing or duplicate Decisions section")
converted = re.sub(r"^allowance: " + allowance + r"$", r"\g<0>\nreturned: none", text, count=1, flags=re.M)
if decisions:
    converted += ("" if converted.endswith("\n") else "\n") + "\n".join(decisions) + "\n"
ledger.write_bytes(converted.encode("utf-8"))
git("add", "--", path)
git("commit", "-q", "-F", "-", "--", path, input=subject + "\n")
PY
```

name: loop-implementation
description: Use after approval selects the loop engine, or when resuming an acceptance-criteria ledger in the implement phase.
---

# Loop implementation

Run this driver in the main session. Carry the absolute implementation worktree path as a value; run git with `git -C "<worktree>"` and commands as `(cd "<worktree>" && <command>)`. Carry the approved spec path and resolved plan directory. Keep the original prompt for verify. Never run reviewers inside implement. Use `plan_tracker({ action: "refresh", path: <absolute ledger path> })` for every refresh; pass only the path and let the extension derive the view. After every admitted ledger commit (child or parent), refresh once; the seed refresh follows implement start below. Read [commit-message.md](../finishing-a-development-branch/reference/commit-message.md) for all commit wording. Resolve its absolute path from this loaded skill and resolve the ticket once at seed or authorized restore; pass `wording: <absolute path>` and `ticket: <reference or none>` to every worker. Use its fixed bookkeeping sentence for each parent event and its amendment source for amendments.

## Entry

1. Read project overrides below. Resolve `gauntlet_setting({ key: "loopEngine" })` and retain `maxIterationsPerRow` (default 4) and `escalateAfter` (default 3). Hold `escalateAfter` in driver memory for this run; never print it or write it to the ledger, and never re-resolve it inside the loop, including after amendment grant re-decodes. Stop on an unavailable settings tool. Select this run's seed value in step 4 and persist it only in the ledger, not in the spec or settings.
2. Resolve verification once using this ordered table. Print `verification command: <command> (<source>)`.

| Observed configuration | Action |
|---|---|
| Overrides `## PR gate` contains `- verification command:` | Use that command; source PR gate. |
| Otherwise overrides has `## verification-before-completion` | Use its exactly one backticked command; zero or several is a configuration error. |
| Neither section supplies a command | Discover the project's test entrypoint from its actual manifest/build instructions; print discovery as source. Stop on an unresolved or ambiguous entrypoint. |

At seed and at an authorized restore, before entering the dispatch loop, read the spec in full. Decode `**Amend-grant:**` through [amendment-surface Value decoding](../brainstorming/reference/amendment-surface.md). Capture the decoded grant, row dispositions, ordered leg membership, each leg's absolute checkout paths and combined spec/task Rules for dispatch and handoff; use home for zero or one leg. At an authorized fresh-session restore, resolve `gauntlet_setting({ key: "loopEngine" })` exactly once at this boundary and hold `escalateAfter` for the run; share that read with reconstruction's Shared allowance boundary, including legacy allowance migration. With an unavailable tool, stop before dispatch with `cannot resolve escalation threshold: settings tool unavailable (loopEngine.escalateAfter)`; never supply an in-loop default.

At seed and at an authorized restore, when the held membership has more than one leg, read `reference/coordinated-legs.md` IN FULL now with read at its absolute path; stop on an unreadable reference naming its path, never reconstruct it. On fresh entry apply its `## Entry` section at step 4 instead of the home-only skeleton below, using step 4's resolved allowance seed value. On a restore apply its `## Resume` section before the dirty-tree stop and before any pending recovery. Keep legacy and single-member ledger bytes unchanged, with no coordinated metadata.

3. Call `phase_tracker({ action: "skip", phase: "plan", reason: "loop engine" })`.
4. Require a clean named-branch implementation worktree. With dirty status and no `pending:` tuple, take ## Human stop before writing the ledger. Read the literal `run allowance: <n>` line from the invoking approval turn: it carries the approved `--allowance=N` flag's value. Use that value over step 1's setting; with no carrier use `maxIterationsPerRow`. Print `allowance: <n> (reply)` or `allowance: <n> (setting)` with the seeded header. Ignore the carrier once a ledger exists; resume uses its header only. Write `<resolved plan dir>/<spec stem>-ledger.md`. Use this grammar with literal values, not placeholders:

```markdown
# Ledger - loop engine
**Spec:** `doc/specs/example.md`
base: <HEAD SHA before skeleton>
verification: <resolved command>
checks: commands
iterations: 0
allowance: <n>
returned: none

| row | status | attempts | evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | open | 0 | |

## Decisions
```

Use the actual repo-relative spec path alone in the Spec header. Read base with `git -C "<worktree>" rev-parse HEAD`. Index every spec AC in order, including nested disposition lines without treating them as extra ACs; keep row text only in the spec. Initialize explicit/absent `in-scope` and `venue:` rows `open`, attempts 0, evidence empty. Initialize only `deviates:`, `deferred:`, `elsewhere:` rows `cut`, attempts 0, disposition text as evidence. Write `allowance:` immediately after `iterations: 0` using step 4's seed value; never scale it by row count or seed dispatches: 24 non-cut rows at default 4 yield allowance 4. All-cut ledgers keep the same allowance and exit through rule 1 without a seed dispatch. Later cuts, reopens and requirement-preserving amendments leave allowance unchanged; redraw deletes the ledger and reseeds it. Serialize evidence in one physical table cell, result lines separated by semicolons, pipes escaped, plain text without angle markup.
5. Call `plan_check({ planPath: <ledger path> })`. Stop with findings as a configuration error. Commit the stamped skeleton with the shared Ledger skeleton sentence; call `phase_tracker({ action: "start", phase: "implement" })`, then `plan_tracker({ action: "refresh", path: <absolute ledger path> })`, including all-cut ledgers with no seed dispatch.

For resume, use the admitted ledger, its base and verification command, and durable iterations and allowance instead of overwriting it. Skip Entry step 1's allowance seeding for an admitted ledger; the allowance setting applies only to fresh seeding, and the restore boundary resolves `escalateAfter` once. Apply `/skill:gauntlet-resume` pending recovery and its allowance and returns conversion steps before refresh and any unresolved dirty-tree stop. Render rows, allowance and decision history; route a recovered pending tuple through reconstruction's pending recovery and ## Interrupted recovery before any unresolved dirty-tree stop.

## Driver holds

After seeding, restrict driver reads during implement to the ledger (including saved or committed ledger snapshots), the child's return file (one file reference), git boundary commands (`status --porcelain`, `rev-list --count`, `rev-parse`, `log -G'^returned: ' --format=%H <base>..HEAD -- <ledger path>`, ledger snapshots via `git show <sha>:<ledger path>`, and `rev-list --reverse --ancestry-path <S>..HEAD` plus `show --format= --name-only <worker sha>` in the tuple's owning checkout), the child's jobs file, OS process start identity and command, `ps -o pgid= -p <pid>`, `kill`, skill resources at their absolute paths and the overrides file. Keep rows by status, iterations, allowance, the last decision, the decoded amendment grant and each leg's checkout path for dispatch, handoff and stops. Use Entry's captured grant, row dispositions and membership throughout the loop.

Never read the spec, source files, test output or logs inside the implement loop. Never diagnose a failure's cause; carry the child's evidence into the next dispatch or human stop. Inside the implement loop, end a turn only with a stop header from ## Human stop; follow every intermediate report with the next ordered-table action in the same turn. The only log-read exception is the last 20 lines at the human stop in After the loop step 1. Leave spec reads for seed, authorized restore and the amendment action below, outside the loop.

## Before each dispatch

When the held membership has more than one leg, read `reference/coordinated-legs.md` IN FULL now with read at its absolute path; stop on an unreadable reference naming its path, never reconstruct it. Apply its `## Resume`, `## Targeting and dispatch`, `## Companion return validation`, `### Companion commit admission` and `## Amendments` sections together with this driver; never apply `## Entry` here.

Read the ledger and require its `checks:` line per ## Gate set.

Require exactly one `returned:` line before each dispatch; without one stop with `ledger has no returned: line - resume through /skill:gauntlet-resume`. Read the ledger and require `allowance:` and no `cap:` before the ordered table, including for seed and completed ledgers; otherwise stop with `ledger has no allowance: line - resume through /skill:gauntlet-resume`. Keep `iterations:` as a dispatch counter only; it bounds nothing. Start each row's window after the later of its latest `row <n> retry` decision and the latest `amended` decision; with neither, start at ledger base. Never reach back past a returns conversion commit. An admitted amendment starts new windows for every row; raising allowance resets neither. Count consecutive validation misses from the window's child `row <n> done|failed` decisions and `repair row <n>` lines excluding those whose second cell starts `interrupted - `: the last two must both be repairs. Recover empty-child windows from ledger snapshots as below, never commit messages. Preserve every row's attempts and spent escalation. Before the ordered table, route each admitted failed target through ## Unreachable returns once at admission (including companions), or on resume when admitted but not yet routed; follow that reference's answered-stop rule after human decisions. Apply this ordered table, starting here after each return or human decision:

| Order | Observed state | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | No `open` or `failed` row | Refresh; require implement complete; continue at ## After the loop step 0. All-cut and baseline-complete ledgers exit here. |
| 2 | Unresolved row attempts >= effective allowance | Human stop with or without amend permission. Exempt `done` and `cut`. |
| 3 | Last two child row commits for the same row changed no file outside the ledger and no row status, or two consecutive validation misses on that row | Set the hint for that row: `the last two attempts changed nothing outside the ledger` for empty-child stagnation, or `two returns broke the contract: <concrete miss from the last repair evidence>` for validation misses; continue to rule 4. |
| 4 | Dispatch allowed | Select target by the priority below, then apply the escalation threshold check. |

Read [empty-child stagnation](./reference/empty-child-stagnation.md) at its absolute path now; stop if unreadable.

When a refresh leaves implement active at rule 1, take the matching human stop; never start verify. Before evaluating rule 2, compute each row's effective allowance as the ledger's `allowance:` plus the count of that row's `row <n> retry | ... | allowed attempts <m>` lines in `## Decisions`. Count each retry once; the stored `<m>` is historical, not an absolute override. Ignore every other decision and grant in this arithmetic. Use the same rule for every coordinated entry, regardless of leg. With allowance 4 and two retries, a row has effective allowance 6 even if the historical `<m>` values are 5 and 99; raising the shared header to 7 makes it 9, while an unretried row gets 7. After migration, a row already at or above its effective allowance is exhausted. Never reset or reduce attempts.

Use the held decoded amendment grant for amendment choices only; ignore its waves-only budget token, retaining no amend permission for a budget-only value. Never consult this value for row escalation. Apply rule 2 before rule 3; a rule-3 hint dispatches through rule 4. Preserve `STAGNANT`, `REJECT` and closureReview boundaries; After the loop step 3 funds conformance rounds from the allowance.

Select `seed` until the ledger at HEAD holds an admitted `row 0 done | seeded ...` decision, independently of `iterations`; before any seed dispatch apply ## Validate the return's seed count instead of rule 3's row windows. Otherwise select the still-unresolved human retry target, then the still-failed row named by the previous decision, then first failed row, then first open row. Read seed completion from the ledger at HEAD, never commit messages or evidence completeness. Never re-seed a validated partial seed to fill empty evidence cells. Use the latest admitted return's target decision for targeting and the child's `previous decision:` input, never an extra's line; skip allowance-grant and legacy grant history while retaining the entire Decisions section. Durable status beats a decision's suggestion. Keep the retry hint only for its target.

For a numbered target with no durable `row <n> escalated` decision, compute `threshold = min(escalateAfter, effective allowance - 1)` from the held `escalateAfter` and the row's effective allowance. When the row's pre-dispatch attempts >= threshold, make this dispatch the escalated round: resolve `gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" })` with or without amend permission. Use the returned non-empty `implModel` string, including the resolver's main-loop model fallback when the setting is unset or malformed. With the settings tool unavailable or `implModel` undefined (neither a configured model nor a main-loop model), stop before dispatch with `Problem: escalationLoop.implModel unavailable`; write no escalation decision and leave attempts unchanged. Never substitute a default-model attempt for that stop.

With the resolved model, append `row <n> escalated | implModel round | allowed attempts <effective allowance>`, commit with the shared Escalation sentence, print `escalated round for row <n>`, and dispatch that attempt with `model: <implModel>` through the normal loop-implementer target, bump and validation path. Exclude this parent commit from child-only stagnation; it starts no new empty-child or validation-miss window. With defaults (allowance 4, `escalateAfter` 3), escalate attempt 4; clamp larger thresholds to the last allowed attempt. At allowance 1, escalate the first and only allowed attempt. A row found past the threshold unspent escalates on its next dispatch. Treat the escalated decision as exactly one round within the effective allowance, never an extra attempt. Recover the row's escalation identity from `## Decisions` on every dispatch and resume; unrecoverable means spent. Preserve `row <n> escalated` for the whole flow across retry, `rows +N`, amendments and resume. Once spent, omit the model override on every later authorized attempt, including every attempt up to a raised effective allowance; never resolve another row escalation or append a second marker. With no marker and recoverable history, apply the threshold predicate after retry or `rows +N`; a previously missing model or migrated row has not spent escalation. Dispatch errors, non-DONE and validation failures consume it before any recommendation decision.

## Dispatch

For home dispatch, record `HEAD_BEFORE`, save the ledger before the iterations bump and tuple write, and retain the current `iterations:` count as i. Send `iteration: i` using the current pre-bump `iterations:` count and write `iterations: i + 1` before dispatch; admission requires the committed ledger's `iterations:` to carry `i + 1`. State that difference when rendering a dispatch or admission: the task carries the pre-bump count, while the ledger and an outside-ledger return's `iteration:` carry the consumed count; never compare them to the task's count. Record the dispatch identity separately and write `pending: <row or seed> | <repo> | <HEAD sha>` using `home` for zero or one spec leg, the actual member identifier for coordinated runs, and the selected checkout's HEAD. Persist the consumed count and tuple before every home or companion dispatch; then refresh. Commit nothing extra. Create a unique absolute output path with `mktemp` outside the repository. Dispatch exactly one foreground child in the main implementation worktree, not a nested worktree:

```text
subagent({ agent: "loop-implementer", context: "fresh", async: false,
  cwd: <absolute implementation worktree>, output: <unique absolute temp path>,
  outputMode: "file-only",
  acceptance: { level: "none", reason: "the parent validates the ledger and the commit" },
  task: "iteration: <i>\nspec: <absolute spec path>\nledger: <absolute ledger path>\nbase: <base SHA>\ntarget: <row number or seed>\nprevious decision: <new conforming line or none>\nhint: <human hint or none>\nwording: <absolute path>\nticket: <reference or none>" })
```

For `target: seed`, explicitly instruct the child to apply its seed contract even when iteration is greater than 0; carry that instruction in the existing `hint` field. Keep the actual consumed pre-bump count in `iteration`.

Omit the model override except on an escalated round (`model: <implModel>`); let the persona override or parent inheritance resolve it. Carry effects only: one file-reference return, one ledger read, git boundary checks. Never read a child transcript or carry reasoning history. Route a dispatch error (including `Request aborted` or any tool-reported `error: <text>`, even with an empty return file) or non-DONE return, including a silence kill, through ## Interrupted recovery. An async handle still stops; never poll or join it. Redispatch only through the ordered table after completed recovery.

## Validate the return

For home returns, apply the following boundary and table. Never project terminal child results before clean/exactly-one-commit admission.
1. Require a DONE return, empty `git -C "<worktree>" status --porcelain` and exactly 1 from `git -C "<worktree>" rev-list HEAD_BEFORE..HEAD --count`. Require the ledger at HEAD to carry the dispatched tuple as its `returned:` value or on a retained `pending:` line, and `iterations:` equal to saved +1. A tuple on neither line is wrong attribution; a retained tuple remains a result-validation miss. Route dispatch errors, non-DONE, killed, dirty, zero/multiple-commit and wrong-attribution returns through ## Interrupted recovery, not result admission. Read result rows and decisions from the ledger at HEAD only after this boundary passes.
2. Validate by dispatched `target`, not iteration number, against the saved copy using this table. Admit exactly three header changes: `iterations` +1, removal of the dispatched `pending:` line and replacement of `returned:` with the dispatched tuple's value; reject every other header change, including allowance. Preserve row identifiers and prior decisions.

| Target | Required changes | Miss |
|---|---|---|
| Seed | Require bounded nonempty evidence on at least one non-cut row; admit a subset or all rows. All attempts stay 0; only `open` -> `done` status transitions; keep unreached rows unchanged, including open rows with empty evidence, and preserve cut rows. Require exactly one new `row 0 done | seeded <k> rows, closed <m> on baseline | <first row to take>` decision, counting only rows given evidence in this return and their proven baseline closures. Partial and complete baseline closure both pass. Never `failed`. | Seed repair below; redispatch seed while its repair count is below allowance. |
| Ordinary | Require the target row's mutable cells to change: status `done` or `failed`, attempts +1, nonempty bounded evidence. Admit zero or more other rows in the same leg changing `open` -> `done`, each with nonempty bounded evidence and attempts unchanged. Require set equality between changed rows and rows with exactly one new decision line, target first, each matching its row and status. Keep every other row, header and prior decision unchanged apart from the dispatch header changes in step 2. | Parent repair below. |
| Seed or ordinary | No committed `pending:` tuple remains. | A retained committed tuple is a validation miss for the dispatched target after boundary admission, not a boundary rejection. |

Require each ordinary decision to match `^row <that row> <that status> \| .{1,200} \| .{1,200}$`; an old conforming line is not a new line. Require check name plus at most three result lines in evidence, serialized with semicolons and escaped pipes as in the persona; add no command-format check. Reject a `failed` extra, a foreign-leg extra, a changed `cut` or `done` row, extra attempts changes, empty evidence on a changed row, or a missing, duplicate, malformed or unmatched decision. Admit an evidenced `done` extra beside a `failed` target. Never police worker ordering or execute a check after a return; leave regressions to verify step 1's gate set. Declare extras only in the ledger diff and their decision lines; inspect no commit message.

On a seed miss after clean/exactly-one-commit admission, restore every non-cut row, headers (including the saved allowance) and decisions from the saved copy; preserve cut rows and retain the incremented iterations. Clear `pending:` and retain the dispatched tuple in `returned:`, setting it when the child retained pending. Append `repair seed | seed miss: <concrete miss> | iteration <consumed>` and commit with the shared Seed repair sentence, then refresh and apply the seed count below. A validated seed resets the validation-miss window, so ordinary dispatch starts clean. Exclude seed repairs from rule 3's row windows.

Count seed attempts as `repair seed` lines in the home ledger, including interrupted and validation-miss repairs; never count commit messages. Dispatch seed while this count is below the ledger allowance, with the seed-contract instruction and `seed miss: <concrete miss>` or `seed interrupted: <reason>` in `hint:`, and `previous decision: none`. Recover the count and reason from those decision lines on resume, using the latest repair's second cell as the hint. At allowance render `Stopped on seed` with `seed: <k> of <allowance>` and the retry/`rows +N` menu; only a raised allowance permits more seed repairs, and a numbered retry never erases this count. Keep row attempts at 0.

On an ordinary miss restore every non-target row, headers (including the saved allowance) and prior decisions from the saved copy, retaining the incremented iterations. Set the target `failed`, attempts = saved attempts +1, evidence = `iteration <i>: <concrete miss>`. Clear `pending:`, keep or set `returned:` to the dispatched tuple, remove malformed appended decisions and append `repair row <n> | <concrete miss> | iteration <consumed>`. Commit with the shared Row repair sentence, then refresh. Set previous decision to `none`; on an admitted ordinary return use the target's new conforming line, never the last extra's. Two consecutive validation misses on a row set its rule-3 hint. A conforming return resets the consecutive-miss count; parent repair commits do not count toward child-only empty stagnation.

## Unreachable returns

Read [unreachable-returns](reference/unreachable-returns.md) in full now with read at its absolute path; apply its evidence routing before returning to the ordered table.

## Interrupted recovery

Read [interrupted recovery](reference/interrupted-recovery.md) in full now; apply its numbered procedure before redispatch.

## Human stop

Read and apply [menu-layout](../brainstorming/reference/menu-layout.md). Start the message with `gauntlet: question` at every human stop, including discard authorization for a dirty tree with no dispatch pending. Put it alone on the first output line, followed by a newline before the stop text, without a driver-state preamble, wrapper or code fence. These decisions are neither done nor stuck outcomes.

Implement-phase stops only: leave implement active and use the row offers below. For verify stops use the menus in After the loop, retaining verify active. Use one screen of plain words: `Stopped on row <n>` for row failures, or the concrete boundary/verification header. `Problem:` quotes the evidence cell and last decision line verbatim; attribute any spec/code contradiction, failing assertion/output or missing capability to that evidence, without investigating it. At every human stop, including allowance, missing-model, dirty-tree and exit-verification stops, list every `open` or `failed` row after the header as `row <n>: <attempts> of <effective allowance>`, then print `Preserve every row's attempts.` Compute each denominator from the ledger using Before each dispatch; keep retry increments in `## Decisions`, never a new table column. Render repaired row cells after recovery, never unadmitted child results. With no open or failed rows, omit row lines but retain the preservation sentence. Name `escalated round spent` when applicable; omit round history and reasoning traces.

For stops not handled by ## Unreachable returns: Offer retry and `rows +N` only at row stops (allowance or missing-model) or seed exhaustion, alongside Amend and Stop. The dirty-tree stop with no dispatch pending keeps discard authorization only, never budget offers; the verify-step-1 verification-failure stop keeps amend/stop only. A budget increase never bypasses those gates.

For non-empty `status --porcelain` with no `pending:` tuple at entry step 4 or on resume, render `Stopped: dirty tree with no dispatch pending`, list the dirty paths, and offer `discard` or Stop only, never budget offers. Before typed discard, make no tree or ledger writes, reset, clean or dispatch. On a typed `discard` run `git -C "<checkout>" reset --hard HEAD` and `git -C "<checkout>" clean -fd`, then resume the sequence the stop suspended: at fresh entry continue Entry step 4's ledger write and step 5 (`plan_check`, skeleton commit, implement start, refresh); on a restore finish eligible migration, final allowance validation and the refresh, then continue at `## Before each dispatch` in implement or `## After the loop` step 1 in verify. Never jump to the ordered table before a ledger is seeded and admitted. Any other reply preserves the tree and keeps the stop open.

| Human choice | Durable action |
|---|---|
| Raise allowance (`rows +N`) | Parse anchored `rows +<n>` with `<n>` matching `[1-9][0-9]*` and a token boundary (end, whitespace or `\|`); reject `rows +50x`. Trim the optional remainder and optional leading pipe into the words cell. Append `rows +<n> \| <words>` under `## Decisions`; bare `rows +50` writes `rows +50 \|`. Raise the shared header allowance by N for every row and leg. Commit both changes exactly once using the shared Allowance raise sentence, leaving iterations and all attempts unchanged; return to the ordered table. For malformed replies, including `rows +0`, `rows +x`, `rows -1` and `rows +50x`, print the accepted forms `retry <n> \| <hint>` and `rows +N` once. On the first and every later invalid reply, keep the same stop open with no writes, commit or dispatch; preserve allowance, decisions, iterations and all attempts. |
| Retry (`retry <n> \| <hint>`) | Parse the row number and hint from that reply. Append `row <n> retry \| <hint> \| allowed attempts <effective allowance + 1>`, commit with the shared Retry sentence, resume checks with that target/hint. Preserve the header allowance, every attempts cell and iterations; increment only that row's effective allowance by one. |
| Amend | Follow `/skill:brainstorming` amendment surface; cut only through an approved disposition amendment. Reconcile ledger and spec in one commit. |
| Stop | Keep phase implement and preserve branch state. |

Serialize the bare decision as `rows +50 |` with an empty words cell. Raising allowance resets neither window (empty-child or validation-miss); exclude allowance-raise commits from child-commit counting. Use Before each dispatch's window rule for retry and admitted amendments.

Recover interrupted returns through ## Interrupted recovery before dispatch, without a human turn. Preserve spent escalation and the consumed dispatch count through recovery: iterations = restored HEAD's value +1, before the next normal bump. Recover from disk/branch, never repeat iteration 0.

Outside the dispatch loop, perform authorized amendment actions under the amendment surface's own reads. After the amendment commit, re-decode the grant and refresh the held row dispositions, membership, checkout paths and Rules from the updated spec before returning to the loop; apply this to funding and standing-grant amendments too. Leave the `**Amend-grant:**` header grammar unchanged.

Retry, cut, amend, raise-allowance and escalate commits never clear the tuple. For ledger amendments use its line-1 discriminant: no plan writer or plan_check; refresh after the amendment commit. Approved deviates/deferred/elsewhere becomes `cut` with disposition evidence; requirement-preserving amendments leave rows unchanged; a re-bounded done row becomes `open` with `reopened by amendment`. Preserve attempts, iterations and allowance. Append `amended | <cut row n, or N item(s)> | <first item title>` and commit spec + ledger with the shared amendment source. Without amend permission, stop for amendments; with amend permission, auto-apply amends. Redraw always stops and deletes the ledger with the plan. Cut only through the amendment surface, including its standing-grant section 5.

End every stop with `Recommendation: <option> - <why>` or `Recommendation: none - <why>`. An unnamed repair is none. Under amend permission take only a named authorized amend: print `took recommendation: amend for row <n>`, apply amendment-surface section 5 (including its audit), record the `amended` decision and commit using the shared amendment source, then return to the ordered table. Whitespace-normalize the row evidence cell and compare with evidence already auto-resolved on that row; repetition renders `Recommendation: none - evidence repeats row <n>`. Recover this evidence from amendment/ledger history; missing history never authorizes a repeated action. A cut leaves the stop; an unresolved row at allowance stops again, not a free retry. Retry, `rows +N` and redraw wait for the human. Fix-first enters `/skill:shape-ticket`'s own gate, never an automatic separate repair. Hard boundaries never auto-take recommendations.

Never invent a stop, a menu, an option or an approval the spec's gate did not ask for, and never write a ruling on what the spec authorizes into a task's `hint:` field.

## Gate set

Require a `checks:` line before each dispatch and at every gate-set site, including finish Step 1. On a missing line stop with `ledger has no checks: line - seeded under the old contract` and offer `stop` only; the human restarts by hand on a fresh baseline. Never migrate, automatically reseed or fall back to `verification:`.

Resolve the set as the deduplicated union of (owning checkout, command) pairs over every non-cut `done` row. Take the command from the first evidence segment up to the first unescaped semicolon; `failed` rows contribute nothing. Order pairs by ledger row number after deduplication: the first row contributing a pair fixes its position. Resolve ownership from the ledger, never the spec: `## Leg mapping` (`row | ac | leg`) names the leg whose checkout owns each expanded row. With no mapping, run every row at home. The same command in two checkouts is two pairs and runs in both, including shared-AC rows. For an all-cut ledger print `gate set empty - every row cut` and continue.

Use the executing process's `LOG_DIR` for every run and rerun: the parent's session directory minted at verify step 0, or the child's own temporary directory per the conformance ledger-subject override. Run each pair as `(cd "<checkout>" && <command>) > "$LOG_DIR/gate-<i>.log" 2>&1`, foreground, one at a time. Print `gate <i> exit <code> <log path>` and keep nothing else from output. Fail-fast: the first nonzero exit ends the run; later pairs do not run. That exit line and log are the single failure for the stop and repair task. Pass only when every pair ran and exited 0. Add no format rule for evidence commands: a non-runnable first segment fails like any command (exit 127 in its log).

Run the complete set at verify step 1, after every whole-diff fix round, at every conformance test site per its ledger-subject override, and at finish Step 1. Only the escalated repair's rerun selects the failing checkout's pairs. Across these sites run zero invocations of the ledger's `verification:` or any leg's `contract:` `- verification:` command; retain the header as the command CI runs. Pass the failing command, its checkout, exit code and log path into later fix-round machinery, never pasted output.

## After the loop

Read SDD's `After All Tasks Complete`, `../subagent-driven-development/reference/happy-path-run.md`, and `../verification-before-completion/reference/conformance-check.md` IN FULL now with read. Stop on an unreadable reference; do not reconstruct it. Execute this continuation, not the waves engine or a generic verification skill:

For coordinated runs, route each verification and review below to every leg with its own base, checkout, Rules and owned original ACs under home flow policy. Re-verify and re-review any changed leg; invoke coordinated finish once from home after every leg passes. Keep single-member/legacy paths free of a companion loop, leg file, `legs:` brief or `--leg` argument.

0. Call `phase_tracker({ action: "start", phase: "verify" })`. Mint `LOG_DIR=$(mktemp -d)` once for this verify session; a resumed session mints a new one at its first gate-set site.
1. Run the gate set per ## Gate set. Require every pair to pass. Commit verification-produced tracked changes, including gate-produced changes, with the shared Verification-produced changes sentence. Any repair invalidates that run: apply the rerun scope below before the next gate. No task reopen/update is awaited.
   Count `repairs` as `repair verification` lines in the home ledger plus one for a `pending: verify` tuple on disk. Use the shared ledger allowance, with no per-row retry increments. Recover this count from the ledger on every resume; the marker appends the decision and clears the tuple together, so one dispatch is never counted twice. Recover an outstanding tuple before any new gate run or dispatch, including the last reserved repair at allowance.
   On failure automatically repair while `repairs < allowance` with or without amend permission; never consult amend permission or gate on iterations. Keep verify active and implement complete. Resolve `gauntlet_setting({ key: "escalationLoop" })`; require its non-empty `implModel`, including the resolver's main-loop fallback. Missing settings/model stops with `Problem: escalationLoop.implModel unavailable`, without a bump or marker. Save the home ledger and home/failing-leg HEADs, then bump iterations once and write `pending: verify | <repo> | <HEAD>` on disk before dispatch, using the failing leg's identity (single-leg `home`) and HEAD. Treat only that bump/tuple as expected home dirt. Dispatch exactly one `implementer` with `model: <implModel>`, `context: "fresh"`, `async: false`, failing checkout cwd and Rules, absolute spec path, failing command, checkout, exit code and log path, never pasted output. Pass the exact pending tuple and consumed `iteration:`, the held `wording:` and `ticket:`, plus the failing leg's base and pre-bump iteration for jobs-file identity. Require a shared-wording repair message with no dispatch state. For a companion repair, prepare a return path through coordinated-legs' Return file section and pass `return:`; require only the tuple and consumed iteration on its first two lines, with no rows or decisions. Inject the persona's step-5 action authorization without its row mutation protocol. Include this blocking-call contract in the repair task: bound every blocking command with `timeout -k 30 <n>`, n <= 600; background and poll longer work. Read [loop-implementer's Evidence command](../../agents/loop-implementer.md#evidence-command) and copy its first three paragraphs verbatim into that task, omitting its row/seed ledger protocol. The repair child reads the log to derive the files to touch; for a stale selector restore the test or its name, never ledger evidence.
   Require DONE, a clean failing checkout and exactly one commit after HEAD_BEFORE. For home attribution require the committed ledger's consumed `iterations:` and retained `pending: verify` tuple; for a companion require that attribution on the return file's first two lines with nothing after them, unchanged home HEAD and only expected bump/tuple dirt. Require all ledger rows, attempts, mapping, allowance, `returned:` and prior decisions unchanged. The home child's sole commit includes the already-bumped ledger with pending retained; a companion commits its leg only. A clean commit with wrong attribution or any protected-state change takes the interrupted path below. Remove `pending:` only in the parent repair marker and append `repair verification | <repo> <child sha7> | iteration <consumed>`. Commit with the shared Verification repair marker sentence, delete the companion return file and refresh. On killed, error, non-DONE, dirty, zero/multiple-commit, wrong-attribution or invalid repair returns, read `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/loop-<failing leg's base SHA>-<pre-bump iteration>.jobs` using the repair task's identity, not home's base, and apply ## Interrupted recovery steps 1-2 to the failing checkout at its saved HEAD. For a companion also reset home to the saved home HEAD with `reset --hard` and `clean -fd`. Write exactly one empty repair marker in home (no repair code): stage only the ledger with saved row cells, saved `returned:`, the already-consumed iteration and no `pending:`. Append `repair verification | <repo> interrupted - <reason> | iteration <consumed>` and commit with the shared Verification repair marker sentence, with no second bump. Delete the companion return file. A non-empty `status --porcelain` after reset blocks neither the marker nor the rerun. Apply interrupted recovery's failure pass with the verification repair count to a failed reset of either checkout or an unwritten marker; require the marker's parent to be the saved home HEAD. On resume, admit a matching clean single repair commit or recover the interrupted return by this same path without another bump; an already admitted matching marker needs no second marker.
   Rerun the failing checkout's gate pairs once using ## Gate set's log redirection and fail-fast rule after each admitted or recovered repair. After that rerun passes, run the original fail-fast run's still-unexecuted pairs from other checkouts in ledger order before recording verified HEAD. On resume run the complete gate set in a fresh session LOG_DIR. A new failure in any leg returns to the repair-count check; do not reopen rows or reset the count. Never spend verify-phase credits. On failure at `repairs >= allowance`, render `Stopped: verification failed with every row closed` with `repairs: <k> of <allowance>` and `Problem:` naming `gate <i> exit <code> <log path>` and quoting at most the last 20 lines with `tail -n 20`; this human-stop excerpt is the driver's only log read. Keep verify active and implement complete; offer amend or stop only, no `Retry with hint` or `rows +N`. Use the same restricted menu for missing capabilities. On success record verified HEAD and clean status for every leg.
2. Dispatch foreground whole-diff `wave-reviewer` per `/skill:requesting-code-review`, from ledger base through committed HEAD, with `SCOPED_TEST_COMMANDS: none`. Apply its fix rounds. Rerun the complete gate set after every fix round before re-review/next gate. Carry final SHIP Minor lines verbatim as `whole-diff minors:`, or `whole-diff minors: none`.
3. Run happy path per the fully read reference when overrides has `## Happy path` or the diff selects a row; use the diff-derived row, not a plan header. Pass summary and outcome to the separate fresh `conformance-reviewer`, along with spec path, verbatim original prompt and full diff. Use spec AC rows against the ledger as the checklist. Follow the reference's partition, concern decomposition, fix rounds and Convergence with the gate set replacing plan Verification at every test site per the reference's ledger-subject override. Use normal conformance Gn tasks on the same tracker and keep durable Gn identities in reports. Rerun the complete gate set after repairs. Resolve closureReview settings and reviewer dispatch per the reference. Reviews happen only after complete implement; none inside the iteration loop.
   When the conformance fix-round cap blocks (`<used> fix round(s) used against a cap of <cap>`) or the reference's step 6 asks at its cap, read `<used>` from that text. Under amend permission with `<used>` below the ledger allowance: when the block is live, call `phase_tracker({ action: "grant_fix_rounds", rounds: <allowance - used>, reason: "<Amend-grant sentence verbatim>" })`, print `funded <allowance - used> conformance rounds under the grant`, and continue the fix loop; when `closureReview.enforce` is false, continue without a call. With `<used>` at or above the allowance, an error reply, or no amend permission, take the reference's step-6 stop. Never call the tool as a probe or store a grant counter; never count rounds yourself. The next block's `<used>` includes granted rounds, so a second block at the allowance stops; a resumed run with unspent credits continues without a block or another grant. Leave the cap and settings unchanged.
   On an approved re-bound (`reopened by amendment`), use the held grant. Without amend permission, refresh and stop with `Stopped: row <n> reopened by amendment during verify`; offer authorize the row's return to ledger implementation or stop. Under amend permission, continue without a second authorization. For the granted continuation or the human-approved return, apply the normal Before each dispatch boundaries, including exhausted-row rule 2, then Dispatch, Validate the return and refresh with verify still active and no phase reset; close on disk and rerun step 1 before continuing verify. During verify, dispatch the reopened row as a one-task `tasks` call carrying the same `## Dispatch` fields (agent, context fresh, async false, cwd, output, outputMode, acceptance, task text, and `model` only on an escalated round), with no `worktree:`; the closure guard counts it as one fix round against the conformance cap funded above. Keep the tuple write, iteration bump, `## Validate the return` and interrupted recovery exactly as for any dispatch. Keep completion blocked until closure; never substitute a tracker write for the ledger return.
4. Complete verify only on current CONFORMS or valid carried-open deferred inventory per the reference. A started positive-cap fix loop blocking/failing/exhausting with an open fix gap stops, never completes verify. Summarize rows closed, iterations consumed, files changed, test counts and review verdict. Emit exact `## Closure / conformance` schema from the reference: `status: CONFORMS (0 open)` or `status: GAPS (N open)`, then `audited-base: <full HEAD SHA>`, happy-path exactly when run, Deferred/deviates per spec exactly when applicable, all gap/concern fields unchanged, auto-applied fix commits index and whole-diff minors. Read its whole-diff-minors companion when directed. Never rename fields.
5. Immediately invoke `/skill:finishing-a-development-branch <abs worktree path>`. Its menu is the human gate; do not add a ready-to-finish prompt.

## Project overrides

If a gauntlet overrides file exists - checked in order: `.pi/gauntlet-overrides.md`, `<repo root>/gauntlet-overrides.md`, `<repo root>/doc/gauntlet-overrides.md`; first found wins - read it once per session - a skill that already has the file's content in context from an earlier skill's read skips the read; a restored session has nothing in context and reads it. Read and apply `## conventions` whenever present, without a relevance judgment. Give this skill's named section precedence over conflicting `## conventions` rules. Use other relevant sections - by name match, by topic (routing, verification, worktrees, etc.), or by workflow convention - to override or extend the instructions above. Project-local `AGENTS.md` is already in context - check it for project-specific routing tables, service paths, and verification commands.

The recognized headings, their readers, and the rules an override cannot change are listed in the [configuration front door](../../README.md#project-specific-overrides); an override extends or replaces the step it names and never lifts this skill's HARD CONSTRAINT or MUST text.
